title: How You'll Know Labour Has Started
hook: Labour usually announces itself with regular, strengthening contractions — sometimes alongside a 'show' or your waters breaking — and then unfolds in three broad stages.
key_points: The clearest sign is contractions: your womb tightens and relaxes, becoming longer, stronger, and more frequent over time.
Other signs include a 'show' (jelly-like pink mucus), backache, or your waters breaking.
Call your midwife when contractions are regular (about every 5 minutes), if your waters break, or if you have bleeding or reduced movements.
Labour has three stages: the cervix opening to fully dilated, pushing and birth, then delivery of the placenta.
content_html: For many first-time parents, the big question is simply: how will I know it's really starting? Labour usually announces itself through contractions — your womb tightening and then relaxing, often feeling like strong period pain — that grow longer, stronger, and more frequent over time. You might also notice a "show" (jelly-like pink mucus), a heavy backache, or your waters breaking.
extra_html: The NHS advises calling your midwife or maternity unit when contractions become regular (around every five minutes), if your waters break, or if you have any bleeding or notice your baby moving less. From there, labour moves through three broad stages: the first, when the cervix softens and opens to fully dilated; the second, the pushing stage that ends with your baby's birth; and the third, when the placenta is delivered. Every labour is different — this is general guidance, and your own midwife or doctor will advise on what's right for your pregnancy and when to come in.

related.title: Why Prenatal Visits Matter
related.hook: Regular checkups during pregnancy catch problems early — for many a typical schedule is monthly, then every two weeks, then weekly as the due date nears.

related.title: Healing After Birth Takes Weeks, Not Days
related.hook: Your body just did something huge, and recovery is a season, not a single appointment. Bleeding, cramps, healing, and mood shifts are all part of the fourth trimester.

flashcards.prompt: What is usually the clearest sign that labour has begun?

choices.text: Regular contractions that get longer, stronger, and more frequent
A single sharp pain that quickly fades

flashcards.explanation_html: Contractions — the womb tightening and relaxing — are the main sign, and they typically build in length, strength, and frequency as labour progresses.

flashcards.prompt: What are the three broad stages of labour?
flashcards.back_html:
1. The cervix opens (dilates) to fully open.
  2. Pushing and birth of the baby.
  3. Delivery of the placenta (afterbirth).

flashcards.prompt: When does the NHS suggest calling your midwife or maternity unit?

choices.text: When contractions are regular (about every 5 minutes), your waters break, or you have bleeding or reduced movements
Only after the baby has been born
Only if you feel completely fine

flashcards.explanation_html: Regular contractions, waters breaking, bleeding, or reduced fetal movement are all reasons to get in touch promptly.
